The customer with a burst pipe at 2 AM has no way to reach the business except a phone call nobody answers.

Missed-call text-back plus after-hours intake. A fast text response bridges the gap between a missed call and a human callback.

Observed pattern: Missed calls are the top universal leak across home-service trades, and fast text-back is the cheapest proven capture mechanism.

The missed call is not the problem. The silence after it is. The customer calls the next shop on the list within minutes.

Missed-call text-back composed on the shop's existing phone system. 10DLC registered, during and after-hours variants, duplicate suppression.

PING says: Do not replace the human. Just make sure the customer gets a human-shaped response before they call the next roofer.

Observed pattern: AI voice answering works as a pilot for shops with genuine after-hours volume, but homeowner preference for humans remains strong and no independent evidence shows voice beating text-back on bookings.

AI answering is a real tool for real after-hours volume, but selling it as the default package fights what homeowners actually want.

Staged combination: text-back as the default package, Sona after-hours intake as a free-to-pilot upsell for volume-qualified Quo clients, with falsification discipline and a live handoff for emergencies.

PING says: We investigated replacing your receptionist with a robot. Good news: we decided not to become the villain.

Observed pattern: Two local businesses publish conflicting phone numbers across their listings. Call tracking is suspected but unconfirmed.

If it is call tracking, the shop is measuring marketing. If it is not, customers are dialing into confusion.

A number audit is a five-minute trust fix, and real call tracking is a legitimate attribution upgrade once Quo's per-number webhooks are in place.
